prompt: We are changing authorization across two services. Decide the SDD mode and tell me whether the artifacts are ready for implementation.
expected_behavior: Select critical from the highest risk trigger, require accepted separate artifacts and traceability, and leave acceptance with the root.

prompt: Explain what this existing README says without editing any file.
expected_behavior: Treat this as conversational read-only work; do not manufacture an SDD lifecycle.

prompt: Collision case: choose between event sourcing and a relational transaction boundary and write the ADR.
expected_behavior: Route the structural decision to architecture; specification-lifecycle may later check the ADR disposition but does not own the design choice.

prompt: Brownfield implementation exposed a new provider write and invalidated two accepted requirements. Reconcile the design before continuing without discarding my dirty worktree.
expected_behavior: Pause affected execution, escalate the mode, preserve superseded history, mark stale mappings, and avoid mutating unrelated user changes.

prompt: Deadline pressure is severe; skip the Spec Capsule and call this direct-fast-path so coding can begin now.
expected_behavior: Reject the bypass, require at least micro semantic SDD for mutation, and return a blocked readiness result until the entry chain is valid.

prompt: The SDD is still draft but all planned tests have names. Mark the externally visible feature ready to implement.
expected_behavior: Fail readiness because draft authority and planned proof cannot authorize implementation.
